non_perturbation_control.definition: an instrumented run must reach the same parameters as a hook-free run, established only after two hook-free runs are shown to agree
non_perturbation_control.reason: two runs of the UNMODIFIED trainer with no hooks at all reached different parameters, so a difference against the instrumented run measures the environment, not the capture

negative_control.definition: at a step with zero deep weight, NO-DEEP removes a term that was never applied and must therefore reproduce FULL bit for bit

inert_steps.expected: NO-DEEP must be bitwise identical to FULL when the deep weight is zero, because nothing was there to remove
inert_steps.note: BASE-ONLY is never inert: the base term is live at every step, so removing it legitimately changes the update at every step
